newsitem.title: UK: UK to merge enviroment and transport ministries.
newsitem.headline: UK to merge enviroment and transport ministries.

text.p: Britain's Labour government said on Wednesday it would merge the environment and transport ministries under Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott.
Gavin Strang is currently the cabinet minister in charge of transport but Prescott has overall control of environment, transport and the regions.
"Significant progress has already been made in integrating the policies of the two Departments," Prescott said in a parliamentary answer.

"To secure the maximum advantage from integration and to simplify lines of responsibility...the Minister for Transport (Strang) and I have concluded that the two Departments should now be merged into a single Department to be known as the Department of the Environment, Transport and the Regions."

The change will take place from June 16. Detailed decisions on organisational structures will not be taken before the end of September and will be preceded by a process of review and consultation with staff and trade unions.
Since Prescott's appointment, the Departments of Environment and Transport have worked in parallel but continued as two separate departments.
